rv.q: But apart from the creative production values, there is not a lot of substance to the play...
It's a study of ambiguity that becomes a master class in obfuscation.
The Meeting: The Interpreter will only work for those already informed of the events depicted in the play.
Indeed, it’s flabbergasting how hard the production works at self-sabotage.
However, I wouldn’t go quite so far as to shout “bravo!” for anything connected with The Meeting: The Interpreter .
Everything is well executed, yet audience members may leave the show wondering if all that activity has any consequence beyond gussying up a rather dry story.
However, I’m completely flummoxed by the play, which explores the June 9, 2016, Trump Tower meeting from multiple angles, literally and figuratively.

cn.t: Critics find this dramatization of the 2016 Trump Tower meeting overwhelmed by excessive multimedia staging and incoherent direction, though Wood and Curran's performances earn praise amid the chaotic production.
